chapters.summary: After Moses' death, God commissions Joshua to lead the Israelites into the promised land, promising to be with him and calling him to be strong and courageous.
keyPoints: God appoints Joshua to succeed Moses, promising to give him the land and to be with him.
Joshua is commanded to carefully keep the law, meditating on it day and night, so that he may prosper and succeed.
Joshua commands the people to prepare to cross the Jordan, and they respond by pledging to obey and follow him.
chapters.application: When facing new challenges, let us, like Joshua, rely on God's promises, be strong and courageous, and carefully keep his word, for God will be with us and give us strength to move forward.

chapters.summary: Joshua sends spies to scout out Jericho, and Rahab the prostitute hides them by faith and is saved, foreshadowing how Gentiles would find grace through faith.
keyPoints: Joshua sends two spies to scout out Jericho, and they enter the house of Rahab the prostitute.
Rahab hides the spies by faith, confessing that the LORD is God in heaven above and on earth below.
The spies give Rahab a scarlet cord as a sign, promising to save her whole family.
chapters.application: Though Rahab was a Gentile, she was saved by faith. Let us respond to God's call in faith rather than by outward appearance or background, for God remembers those who trust in him.

chapters.summary: Joshua leads the Israelites across the Jordan River as God causes the water to stand up in a heap, showing that he is with Joshua just as he was with Moses.
keyPoints: Joshua commands the people to consecrate themselves, for the next day God would do wonders among them.
The priests carry the ark ahead of the people, and as soon as their feet touch the water, the river's flow is cut off, and the people cross on dry ground.
God exalts Joshua in the sight of the people, and they revere him just as they had revered Moses.
chapters.application: When you face obstacles that seem impossible, trust God—he will make a way for you. Consecrate yourself first, follow his leading, and he will be with you.

chapters.summary: Joshua 4 records how, after crossing the Jordan, the Israelites set up stones as a memorial at God's command, commemorating how he dried up the river and led his people into the promised land.
keyPoints: The Israelites take twelve stones from the Jordan and set them up at Gilgal as a memorial.
Joshua also sets up twelve stones in the riverbed itself, symbolizing the twelve tribes of Israel.
God parts the waters of the Jordan just as he had parted the Red Sea, showing his presence and power.
chapters.application: In everyday life, let us continually remember God's grace, setting up our own spiritual 'stones' to remind ourselves and future generations to rely on his power in times of difficulty.

chapters.summary: Joshua 5 records how the Israelites were circumcised at Gilgal, kept the Passover, and how Joshua met the commander of the LORD's army—events marking the formal moment when a new generation of Israelites took possession of the promised land.
keyPoints: When the kings of Canaan hear that the Israelites had crossed the Jordan, their hearts melt and their courage fails.
At Gilgal, the Israelites circumcise all the males, rolling away the reproach of Egypt.
The people keep the Passover, and the next day they eat the produce of the land; the manna ceases, and Joshua sees a vision.
chapters.application: God is with us at every new stage of life. Let us respond to his call with obedience and reverence, taking each step by faith.

chapters.summary: Joshua leads the Israelites around Jericho for seven days; the walls collapse and the city is destroyed, and only Rahab the prostitute and her family are spared.
keyPoints: Following God's instructions, the Israelites march around the city for seven days, and on the seventh day, at their great shout, the walls fall down.
The city is utterly destroyed, but Rahab and her family are saved because of her faith and are brought into the community of Israel.
Joshua pronounces a curse on anyone who would rebuild Jericho, demonstrating God's judgment and sovereignty.
chapters.application: When circumstances seem impossible, let us obey God in faith, for he will make a way; and let us remember his grace, as Rahab did, finding salvation through faith.

chapters.summary: Because of Achan's sin, Israel is defeated at Ai; Joshua cries out to God in mourning, God reveals the cause, Achan is exposed and punished, and Israel is restored to victory.
keyPoints: Because Achan disobeys God's command, the Israelites are defeated at Ai, and their morale is shattered.
Joshua mourns and inquires of God, who reveals that devoted things have been kept back, and the people must consecrate themselves and remove the sin.
Achan confesses his sin, he and his family are put to death, and Israel is restored to holiness and attacks again.
chapters.application: When we meet setbacks in life, let us first examine ourselves for hidden sin, be honest with God, and remove whatever defiles us, so that we may be renewed in strength.

chapters.summary: Joshua leads the Israelites to take Ai by strategy, following God's instructions to set an ambush and utterly destroy the city, then builds an altar to God on Mount Ebal and renews the law.
keyPoints: God tells Joshua not to be afraid, but to take all the fighting men and attack Ai, promising to deliver the city and its king into his hand.
Joshua sets an ambush west of the city, draws the enemy out, and the ambush rises up to take the city, setting it on fire and destroying it completely.
The Israelites build an altar on Mount Ebal and offer sacrifices, copy the law onto stones, and read aloud the blessings and curses to the people.
chapters.application: When we face failure, let us turn back and seek God, listening to his guidance, and we will find fresh strength to overcome the challenge.

chapters.summary: Joshua 9 records how the Gibeonites deceive the Israelites into making a treaty with them; Israel is fooled because they fail to inquire of the LORD, but in the end they keep their word.
keyPoints: Hearing of Israel's victories, the Gibeonites disguise themselves as envoys from a distant country, wearing worn-out clothes and sandals and carrying dry, moldy bread.
Without inquiring of the LORD, the Israelites make a treaty with the Gibeonites based on appearances, only to discover afterward that they had been deceived.
Joshua and the leaders keep their oath, letting the Gibeonites live, but they are made woodcutters and water carriers.
chapters.application: When making important decisions, let us first pray and seek God's guidance rather than relying on our own judgment, so that we do not fall into a trap.

chapters.summary: Joshua leads the Israelites to defeat a coalition of five Amorite kings, and his prayer causes the sun to stand still, displaying God's mighty power.
keyPoints: The Gibeonites seek peace, and Joshua, bound by treaty, comes to their defense.
Five kings join forces to attack Gibeon; Joshua marches to the rescue, and God sends hailstones to fight for Israel.
Joshua prays for the sun to stand still, and Israel wins a great victory, capturing and killing the five kings.
chapters.application: When facing difficulty, let us trust God as Joshua did, praying boldly, for he will fight for us and turn the impossible into the possible.

chapters.summary: Joshua leads the Israelites to defeat a coalition of northern kings and takes their land, destroying all the inhabitants as God had commanded, completing the conquest of Canaan.
keyPoints: The northern kings join forces, with an army as numerous as the sand of the seashore, and camp by the waters of Merom.
God tells Joshua not to be afraid, promising to hand the enemy army over to Israel.
Joshua captures the cities and kills the kings, destroying all the inhabitants, though as God commanded he keeps the livestock and plunder.
chapters.application: When facing difficulties that seem overwhelming, let us trust God's promises rather than our own strength, obeying his word completely, and we will be more than victorious.

chapters.summary: This chapter lists the kings the Israelites defeated on both sides of the Jordan, summarizing the results of the conquest.
keyPoints: It lists the two kings defeated by Moses east of the Jordan and how their land was allotted.
It lists the thirty-one kings defeated by Joshua west of the Jordan, covering territories throughout the north and south.
It emphasizes that Israel's possession of the land was the fulfillment of God's promise.
chapters.application: Looking back at the victories God has given in the past strengthens our faith; when we face today's challenges, let us remember that he will surely fulfill his promises.

chapters.summary: When Joshua is old, God instructs him to allot the land not yet conquered to the tribes of Israel as their inheritance, and the chapter lists both the unconquered territory and the land already divided.
keyPoints: Joshua is now old, and God commands him to divide the remaining land among nine and a half tribes.
The unconquered territories are listed in detail, including the regions of the Philistines, the Canaanites, and others.
The tribe of Levi receives no land, for the LORD himself is their inheritance.
chapters.application: Even when we are old or facing unfinished tasks, God remains faithfully at work. Let us receive his promises in faith, make him our ultimate inheritance, and serve him faithfully for the rest of our lives.

chapters.summary: Joshua 14 records the beginning of the land distribution in Canaan and how Caleb received Hebron as his inheritance by faith.
keyPoints: As God commanded, the Israelites divide the land west of the Jordan at Gilgal by casting lots.
The Levites receive no inheritance of land but are given towns with pasturelands, for the LORD is their inheritance.
True to his word, though now old, Caleb asks for Hebron, and because he had wholeheartedly followed God, he receives it.
chapters.application: No matter our age, if we wholeheartedly follow God, we will receive the inheritance he has promised. Let us follow Caleb's example, facing challenges with faith and holding fast to the end.

chapters.summary: Joshua 15 records in detail the boundaries and towns of Judah's inheritance, along with the accounts of Caleb capturing Hebron and Othniel capturing Debir.
keyPoints: The boundaries of Judah's territory are clearly described from south to north, including wilderness, hill country, and lowland regions.
As promised, Caleb drives out the descendants of Anak and captures Hebron, and gives his daughter Achsah in marriage to Othniel.
Othniel captures Debir, and Achsah asks Caleb for springs of water, showing how faith and blessing are passed on.
chapters.application: Let us learn from Caleb's faith, laying hold of God's promises without shrinking back from difficulty, and be willing to pass on our blessings to the next generation.

chapters.summary: This chapter describes the boundaries of the inheritance given to the descendants of Joseph—Ephraim and the half-tribe of Manasseh—emphasizing that they received their inheritance according to God's promise.
keyPoints: The land given to Joseph's descendants stretches from the Jordan to the Mediterranean Sea, including towns such as Shiloh.
The boundaries of Ephraim's territory are described in detail, its southern border touching Benjamin's.
Canaanites still live in Gezer, but they are put to forced labor rather than being fully driven out.
chapters.application: The promises God gives us must be received in faith and carried out faithfully. When facing unfinished work, let us keep relying on God to press forward, not shrinking back because of difficulty.

chapters.summary: This chapter records how the half-tribe of Manasseh and the tribe of Ephraim receive their inheritance, along with the account of Zelophehad's daughters receiving a portion of land.
keyPoints: The half-tribe of Manasseh receives its inheritance west of the Jordan, including Gilead and Bashan.
Because Zelophehad had no sons, his daughters receive an inheritance according to God's instruction, setting a precedent for women's right to inherit.
The descendants of Joseph ask for more land, and Joshua encourages them to clear the forested hill country and drive out the Canaanites.
chapters.application: When we feel that what we have is not enough, let us, like the descendants of Joseph, actively press forward, trusting the strength God gives, and boldly face challenges to enlarge our territory.

chapters.summary: Joshua sets up the tabernacle at Shiloh and sends out surveyors to map the unclaimed land, dividing an inheritance among the remaining seven tribes.
keyPoints: The Israelites gather at Shiloh, where the tabernacle is set up, establishing the center of worship.
Joshua instructs the seven remaining tribes to send three men each to survey the land, so that it can be divided by lot according to God's will.
Benjamin receives the first allotment of land, and its boundaries and towns are recorded in detail.
chapters.application: When facing unfinished tasks, let us follow Joshua's example—first seeking God's guidance, then planning together in unity, dividing responsibilities according to his will, and blessing will follow.

chapters.summary: Joshua 19 records the territories given to Simeon, Zebulun, Issachar, Asher, Naphtali, and Dan, and the town Joshua finally receives as his own inheritance.
keyPoints: Simeon receives its inheritance within Judah's territory, since Judah's portion had been more than it needed.
Zebulun, Issachar, Asher, and Naphtali each receive their land by lot.
After Dan receives its inheritance, Joshua is given the town of Timnath-serah as his own.
chapters.application: God faithfully gave the promised land to each tribe. Let us likewise trust God's arrangement of our lives, humbly receiving the portion he gives us.

chapters.summary: Joshua 20 records the LORD's instructions to Joshua to establish six cities of refuge, providing shelter for anyone who kills another by accident until they can stand trial before the assembly.
keyPoints: The LORD commands Joshua to establish cities of refuge, so that anyone who kills someone accidentally can flee there for safety.
Anyone fleeing to a city of refuge must explain the case at the city gate, and the elders take them in.
The city of refuge provides protection until the death of the high priest, at which point the one who fled may return home.
chapters.application: In life we sometimes make mistakes, but God provides a refuge. When we face trouble or failure, let us seek his shelter and trust in his justice and mercy, finding true rest and forgiveness in Christ.

chapters.summary: Joshua 21 records how the Levites received towns and pasturelands from the other tribes, and how every land God had promised to Israel was now given.
keyPoints: The Levites receive forty-eight towns with their pasturelands throughout Canaan as their inheritance.
These towns are scattered among the other tribes, enabling the Levites to teach the law throughout Israel.
Every promise God had made to give Israel the land was fulfilled; not one word failed.
chapters.application: God is faithful, and he will fulfill his promises. Let us, like the Levites, serve faithfully wherever he has placed us, trusting his provision and guidance.

chapters.summary: Joshua 22 records how Joshua blesses the two and a half tribes and sends them back east of the Jordan; the altar they build there causes a misunderstanding, which is finally resolved through honest communication, preserving Israel's unity.
keyPoints: Joshua charges the two and a half tribes to carefully keep the commandments and love God faithfully, then sends them home with his blessing and great wealth.
The tribes east of the Jordan build a large altar by the river, and the tribes west of the Jordan, fearing this is a betrayal of God, are alarmed.
After the matter is explained, everyone understands the altar was built as a witness, not for sacrifice, and the dispute ends in rejoicing.
chapters.application: In our life of faith, when misunderstandings arise, let us follow the example of the eastern tribes—explaining ourselves openly and resolving disagreements with love and honesty, preserving unity within the church.

chapters.summary: Near the end of his life, Joshua gathers the leaders of Israel, urging them to keep God's law carefully and love him alone, and warning of the consequences of forsaking him.
keyPoints: Now old, Joshua summons all Israel and its leaders to deliver God's word to them.
He reviews God's promises and mighty acts, urging the people to be strong and courageous and to carefully obey the law of Moses.
He warns them not to mix with the surrounding peoples or worship their idols, for if they do, God will no longer drive out the nations before them and will instead bring disaster upon them.
chapters.application: Let us continually remember God's faithfulness, carefully keep his word, stay far from the temptations of the world, and love the Lord wholeheartedly, following him all our lives.

chapters.summary: Joshua gathers all the tribes of Israel at Shechem, recounts God's grace from the days of Abraham onward, and makes a covenant with the people, calling them to serve the LORD alone.
keyPoints: Joshua reviews God's acts throughout history, from the calling of Abraham to the exodus from Egypt and the entry into Canaan.
The people twice affirm their commitment to serve the LORD, and Joshua warns them that they cannot serve him alongside idols.
Joshua makes a covenant with the people, sets up a stone as a witness, and afterward dies and is buried within his own inheritance.
chapters.application: Let us remember God's guidance throughout our lives, resolve each day to follow the Lord alone, and bear witness to our faith through concrete action in our families and daily lives, passing it on to the next generation.
